items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: And I got to play with him too and record with him two or three times because of a similar status that I enjoyed at Prestige Records.

ctx.x: No, no, no, no. I didn’t meet Hawk until I came to New York. And I got to play with him too and record with him two or three times because of a similar status that I enjoyed at Prestige Records. A record date, they would call me sometimes, once in a while, and the dates with Coleman Hawkins were wonderful, beautiful, wonderful.

So as a house pianist, if the manager said to you okay — how much warning did you have, or I wouldn’t say warning, how much time did you have before you knew a particular guy was coming to play, and did you feel you had to do some homework somehow to research the tunes that you knew that they liked to play? Or did you just have enough knowledge at that time where you could go in.
